City of [[Haugesund]], [[Rogaland]] | capacity = 8,754 | chairman = Christoffer Falkeid | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Endre Eide]] | league = [[1. divisjon]] | season = [[2025 Eliteserien|2025]] | position = [[Eliteserien]], 16th of 16 (relegated) | website = {{official URL}} | current = 2024 FK Haugesund season | pattern_la1 = _haugesund1617h | pattern_b1 = _haugesund1617h | pattern_ra1 = _haugesund1617h | pattern_sh1 = _haugesund1617a | pattern_so1 = _haugesund18h | leftarm1 = ffffff | body1 = ffffff | socks1 = ffffff | pattern_la2 = _haugesund1617a | pattern_b2 = _haugesund1617a | pattern_ra2 = _haugesund1617a | pattern_sh2 = _haugesund1617a | pattern_so2 = _haugesund20a | leftarm2 = 0000ff | body2 = 0000ff | rightarm2 = 0000ff | shorts2 = FFFFFF | socks2 = 0000ff }} '''Fotballklubben Haugesund''' ({{lit|Football Club Haugesund}}), usually referred to as '''FK Haugesund''' or '''FKH''', is a professional [[association football|football]] club from the city of [[Haugesund]] that plays in the second tier of the [[Norwegian football league system]]. FK Haugesund previously played in the top division in 1996–1998, 2000 and in 2010–2025. The club have been runners-up in the [[Norwegian Cup]] in 2007 and 2019 as well as having competed in the qualifying stages for the [[UEFA Europa League]] in 2014–15, 2017–18 and 2019–20. The club's best achievement in the national league is the [[bronze medal]] in Eliteserien in 2013, and fourth place in the 2016 and 2018-seasons. It was originally founded on 28 October 1993 after a merger between the Haugesund-based football clubs [[SK Djerv 1919|Djerv 1919]] and [[SK Haugar]]. The club plays its home matches at the [[Haugesund Stadion]] near the city-centre of Haugesund. The stadium has a capacity of 8,754. ''Maakeberget'' is the official but independent supporter club of FK Haugesund."}}
